# The definition of "required for merge" for vidra-core.
#
# scripts/ci/require-checks.sh reads this file in the `ci-required` job and
# fails unless every entry is satisfied for the commit under test. Configure
# ONE required status check in branch protection — `ci-required` — and this
# file becomes the single place the required set is declared and reviewed.
#
# Syntax (one check-run name per line, i.e. a job's name as GitHub reports it):
#   name    must EXIST for this commit and must conclude `success`
#   ?name   required only IF it ran (path-filtered lanes)
#
# Nothing but `success` passes: `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `neutral` and
# `skipped` all fail, so a lane cannot be waved through by being interrupted.

# backend-ci.yml — the canonical `make ci` gate (fmt, vet, migrate-lint,
# openapi-verify, sqlc-verify, race unit tests) + exact module manifest.
build-test

# backend-integration.yml — `-tags=integration` against real Postgres, Redis,
# ffmpeg, clamd and MinIO, with the no-silent-skip audit over its verbose log.
integration

# openapi.yml — Redocly lint + route/spec drift guard. This spec is what the
# separate vidra-user repo generates its client from, so drift here breaks a
# repo that cannot see this PR.
openapi

# ipfs-integration.yml — local-kubo add/pin/cat and HLS-tree gateway proofs.
# (The public-gateway round trip is deliberately NOT required; it runs in the
# scheduled ipfs-public-gateway lane.)
ipfs-integration

# ipfs-private-integration.yml — private-swarm isolation proofs. All-local
# dependencies and IPFS_PRIVATE_PROOFS_REQUIRED=1, so it is deterministic.
ipfs-private-integration

# vuln.yml — govulncheck: fails when this module's code reaches a known Go
# vulnerability, or when the scan cannot run. Not path-filtered and re-run
# daily, because new vulnerabilities arrive without a commit. TWIN in both Go repos.
govulncheck

# ci-guard.yml — action pins, no hidden continue-on-error, backend-ci really
# runs `make ci`. Path-filtered to .github/workflows/**, so required only when
# a workflow changed — which is exactly when it has anything to say.
?guard

# rollback-floor.yml — the PREVIOUS release's migrator against this schema.
# Path-filtered to migrations/, internal/dbmigrate/ and cmd/api/migrate.go.
?prev-migrator-against-new-schema

# schema-compat.yml — the previous release's integration suite against this
# schema (~45 min). Path-filtered to migrations/; cadence unchanged.
?prev-release-against-new-schema

# NOT required, deliberately, and each one says why in its own workflow header:
#   bench                          bench-fuzz.yml, scheduled exploratory signal
#   fuzz                           bench-fuzz.yml, scheduled exploratory signal
#   ipfs-public-gateway            depends on a third party's availability
#   assets / publish               release-triggered, not PR gates
